Error.description: Campus error envelope (see ErrorEnvelope); malformed or invalid fields use the ValidationError shape (422, with error.errors). Possible statuses: 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 415, 422, 429, 500, 503.

code.description: Campus error code (UPPER_SNAKE_CASE; AUTH_* for OAuth protocol errors, RFC 6749 §5.2)

details.description: Additional error details, including OAuth protocol fields (error, error_description)

errors.description: Field-level validation errors; present on the 422 ValidationError shape only

code.description: Machine-readable field error code, e.g. MISSING, INVALID_TYPE, UNRECOGNIZED_FIELD

info.description:
Observability backend for Campus: trace/span ingestion, querying, journey grouping, and audit API-key management.

The /audit/v1 endpoints require Bearer authentication with an audit API key (audit_v1_<22-char-base64url>). The audit web UI lives in the campus-admin portal, which consumes this API with its own key; this service redirects the UI's old page URLs there (AUDIT_UI_URL).

## Trailing slashes

Paths are listed exactly as routed (Flask): a path shown with a trailing slash must be requested with it — the no-slash variant answers with a 308 redirect.
info.title: Campus Audit API

get.summary: Send old UI URLs to the portal (or explain where it moved).

get.description:
Query params:
    owner_id: Filter by owner ID (optional)
    active_only: Only show active (non-expired, non-revoked) keys (default: true)
    limit: int, default 50

Returns:
    List of API key summaries (excluding key_hash)
get.summary: List API keys with optional filtering.

post.description:
Request body:
{
  "name": "string",
  "owner_id": "string",
  "scopes": ["scope1", "scope2"],  // optional
  "role": "traces-viewer",  // optional, a named role (#918)
  "rate_limit": 100,  // optional, requests per minute
  "expires_at": "ISO 8601"  // optional
}

Give either a role or a list of scopes, not both: a role is a named
bundle of scopes from the catalogue (campus.audit.roles), and
naming both leaves it ambiguous which one was meant.

Returns:
    201 Created with the API key (only shown once) and key details
    422 Unprocessable Entity on invalid input

delete.description:
This marks the API key as revoked. It will no longer work for
authentication, but the record is kept for audit purposes.

Args:
    api_key_id: The API key identifier

Returns:
    204 No Content on success
    404 Not Found if API key doesn't exist

get.description:
Args:
    api_key_id: The API key identifier

Returns:
    Full API key details (excluding key_hash)
get.summary: Get a specific API key by ID.

patch.description:
Only name, scopes, and rate_limit can be updated.
Use DELETE to revoke an API key.

Args:
    api_key_id: The API key identifier

Request body:
{
  "name": "new name",  // optional
  "scopes": ["scope1", "scope2"],  // optional
  "role": "traces-viewer",  // optional, a named role (#918)
  "rate_limit": 200  // optional
}

Give either a role or a list of scopes, not both: a role is a named
bundle of scopes from the catalogue (campus.audit.roles), and
naming both leaves it ambiguous which one was meant.

Returns:
    200 OK with updated API key details
    404 Not Found if API key doesn't exist
    422 Unprocessable Entity on invalid input
patch.summary: Update mutable fields of an API key.

post.description:
Creates a new plaintext API key value while keeping the same ID.
The old key will no longer work after regeneration. The new key
is returned in the response and will not be shown again.

Args:
    api_key_id: The API key identifier

Returns:
    200 OK with the new API key (shown only once) and updated details
    404 Not Found if API key doesn't exist
post.summary: Regenerate an API key with a new value.

Args:

Returns:

get.description:
Query params:
    since: ISO 8601 timestamp (optional)
    until: ISO 8601 timestamp (optional)
    limit: page size, clamped to [1, MAX_PAGE_SIZE] (default
        DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE)
    cursor: opaque token from a previous page's cursor.next

Supports content negotiation via Accept header:
    - application/json: Structured JSON with cursor pagination
    - text/plain: Compact human-readable text

Returns:
    JSON: {"traces": [...], "cursor": {"next": "...", "has_more": true}}
    Text: Compact trace list with pagination hint

post.description:
Accepts a single span or batch of spans. Returns 201 Created on full
success, or 207 Multi-Status on partial failure with per-span status
indicators.

Request body:
{
  "spans": [
    {
      "trace_id": "string",
      "span_id": "string",
      "parent_span_id": "string | null",
      "method": "string",
      "path": "string",
      "status_code": 200,
      "started_at": "ISO 8601",
      "duration_ms": 142.5,
      "query_params": {},
      "request_headers": {},
      "request_body": null,
      "response_headers": {},
      "response_body": null,
      "client_id": "string | null",
      "user_id": "string | null",
      "api_key_id": "string",
      "client_ip": "string",
      "user_agent": "string",
      "error_message": "string | null",
      "tags": {}
    }
  ]
}

Returns:
    201 Created with span IDs on success
    207 Multi-Status on partial failure
    400 Bad Request on invalid input
    429 Too Many Requests when a rate-limit bucket is exceeded
        (#831); the response carries Retry-After and the tripped
        bucket key in the error details

Note:
    Audit events are emitted for both successful ingestions (201/207)
    and validation failures (400) via the @audit_event decorator.
    The decorator uses flask.after_this_request to capture the final
    response after error handlers run, so failed ingestions are logged
    with error details.

get.description:
Query params:
    path: Filter by endpoint path
    status: Filter by HTTP status code
    api_key_id: Filter by API key
    client_id: Filter by OAuth client
    user_id: Filter by user
    journey_id: Filter by login-journey tag (#803)
    since: ISO 8601 timestamp (optional)
    until: ISO 8601 timestamp (optional)
    limit: page size, clamped to [1, MAX_PAGE_SIZE] (default
        DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE)
    cursor: opaque token from a previous page's cursor.next
    events: include audit-event traces (spans tagged with an
        event_type, #941). Default is to include them, as this
        endpoint always has; callers that want the viewer's
        request-only list (event trails are noise when debugging a
        real flow) pass events=false. true/1 and false/0 are the
        accepted literals; anything else is a field error.

Supports content negotiation via Accept header.

Returns:
    Filtered trace list matching criteria with cursor pagination

Args:
    trace_id: The 32-char hex trace identifier

Supports content negotiation via Accept header:
    - application/json: Nested tree structure with children arrays
    - text/plain: Waterfall with offset timing

Returns:
    JSON: {"trace_id": ..., "root_span": <trace tree with nested children>}
    Text: Waterfall visualization showing timing hierarchy
